annotationRationale: Coordinate reflections and rotations identify the ten groups of cell positions that must share a color. The multiplication principle counts the two independent color choices for each group.
sourceMethod: Followed the official orbit-coloring method. Replaced its unavailable labeled diagram with center coordinates to justify the ten orbits and the uniqueness of each coloring.

review.mathCheck: The required symmetries give exactly the signed coordinate permutations. Their cell orbits have unique representatives 0 ≤ b ≤ a ≤ 3, giving 1+2+3+4=10 orbits, including the center, axes and diagonals. Independent binary choices give 2^10 colorings; excluding the two monochromatic grids leaves 1022, choice B. The explanation is complete and appropriate for AMC 12.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, independently worded adaptation of official solution 15's orbit method on page 8. The coordinate representatives establish the same ten groups labeled A through J in the official figure, followed by the same independent color choices and exclusions.
review.annotationCheck: All three selected concepts are directly used. No material annotation repair is needed. The unselected math:symmetry-counting concerns identifying arrangements under symmetry, whereas this problem counts colorings invariant under every required symmetry.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The three exact native links appropriately cover axis-reflection coordinates, rotation correspondences and the multiplication principle. They support these named steps, without claiming national coverage of the additional cell-orbit argument.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 8.G.A.3 and 6.NS.C.6b support the coordinate-reflection step. G-CO.A.4 supplies rotation-definition background, rather than demonstrated definition development. No US link is supplied for cnm_h231 or the orbit-counting technique.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: cnm_136 supports sign changes, cnm_244 supports rotational correspondences, and cnm_h231 supports multiplying the ten binary choices. All are appropriate assessed components; none is merely contextual. Formal group theory is unnecessary.
